title: ASIC warns scammers are using AI to spin vast webs of deception

reading.body:
An AI system was used to create a deepfake article falsely attributing statements to a Reserve Bank governor and a well-known finance presenter, in order to impersonate them and promote an unlicensed cryptocurrency trading platform. The system generated convincing fabricated news content as part of a broader scam infrastructure that included fake reviews and advertisements. This represents an impersonation deployment, where the technology was used to make false statements appear to come from real people.

The failure to catch this happened at the point of publication and distribution. No human verification appears to have occurred before the fake article reached potential victims. A check against the actual publication records of the outlets being impersonated, or confirmation from the real people allegedly quoted, would have exposed the fabrication.

It is not established whether the AI system was purpose-built for this fraud, whether the platform hosting it knew of the use, or what technical measures could have prevented this particular deployment.

reports.title: The fake Alan Kohler interview that shows a type of scam that’s on the rise
AI deepfake scams 'an emergency in the making' as ASIC reports rise in false investment endorsements
ASIC warns scammers are using AI to spin vast webs of deception

summary:
# Summary

A fake online article claimed that Reserve Bank governor Michele Bullock had a heated interview with ABC finance presenter Alan Kohler about Boulder Sparhaven, an unlicensed cryptocurrency trading platform. The interview never actually occurred. This fabricated story represents a growing type of scam that uses artificial intelligence to create convincing deepfake content featuring well-known Australians. ASIC reports that such investment scams are becoming increasingly common and sophisticated, with the regulator taking down 19,400 scams last year, a 182 percent increase from the previous year.

The scammers impersonate prominent figures including Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, businessperson Dick Smith, and wealthy mining magnate Gina Rinehart to build fake investment opportunities. They create elaborate webs of deception using fabricated news articles, fake reviews, and advertisements to lure consumers. ASIC advises people to verify Australian Financial Services licence numbers through their public registers before investing. Presenter Alan Kohler argues that platforms and AI companies should face heavy fines for enabling such scams.
